newsitem.title: USA: Alleged U.S. bomb mastermind surrenders.
newsitem.headline: Alleged U.S. bomb mastermind surrenders.

text.p: The alleged mastermind behind two bombings in a northern California town surrendered peacefully to police on Monday as the number of suspects arrested in the case rose to six, police said.
Kevin Robinson, 29, gave himself up in Vallejo, 35 miles (50 km) northeast of San Francisco, after his attorney made arrangements for his surrender, officials said.
Police had been searching for Robinson, wanted on suspicion of conspiracy and explosives violations. They had said he should be considered armed and dangerous.

Vallejo police spokesman Lt. Ron Jackson said police believed Robinson hired two other men to carry out the bombings to disrupt his trial on drugs charges that had been due to start in a nearby town on Monday.
"We think it was a bombing for hire," Jackson said.
Jackson said a total of six people had been arrested in connection with two bombings in Vallejo in the last 10 days that damaged a courthouse and a bank but caused no injuries.
Police disarmed a third bomb containing at least 30 sticks of dynamite found on Jan. 25 outside a public library that also housed a police evidence room.
Army Osotonu, 34, his brother Oston Osotonu, 24, and Francis Ernestberg, 40, were arrested on Sunday. All were booked into the county jail for investigation of conspiracy and explosives charges.
Two other suspects, Orlando Johnson, 30, and Jason Pascual, 22, were arrested on Monday, police said.
Local television showed FBI agents, wearing military-style fatigues and helmets and carrying rifles, leading one suspect out of a house.

Jackson said he did not think there were any more suspects still at large. He said police were "pretty comfortable" they had recovered all of a large amount of dynamite stolen from a construction site, some of which was allegedly used in the bombings.
"I think we've pretty much got the case closed. As catastrophic as this could have been, we're very pleased that no one got injured," he said.
Between 75 and 100 local, state and federal officials investigated the bombings, Jackson said.
Robinson was due to go on trial on Monday on charges of possession or possession for sale of marijuana, cocaine and heroin, his attorney Daniel Russo said.
Since he has previous convictions, a conviction on these charges could have brought Robinson a life prison term under California's "three strikes and you're out" law, police said.

"It's our opinion that he has conspired with these other individuals in an effort to do whatever he possibly can do to stop his trial from starting today," Vallejo police chief Robert Nichelini told reporters.
Russo said he arranged Robinson's surrender with police after speaking with his client Monday. He said Robinson wanted to surrender but was concerned he would be killed in the process.

Russo said he picked Robinson up and took him to a site in south Vallejo where he said police were waiting with snipers and a SWAT team. "They handcuffed him. It went very smoothly," he told Reuters. He said Robinson had worked as a rap music producer and had three children.

On Sunday, police seized 500 lbs (230 kg) of dynamite stored in a Vallejo garage and found a car with 61 sticks of dynamite in the trunk that investigators believe the bombers had wired up ready for use in another attack.
Authorities say the Vallejo bombings are not connected to three mail bombs found in the San Diego area in recent days.
